title: UNECA: internet shutdowns and open blocking of social media reported in Ethiopia
publisher_or_author: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)
institution: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
claim: UNECA's digital trade country profile reports that it is common for the Ethiopian government to openly block some social media sites like Telegram or to shut down telecom and internet services, that government authorities imposed a nationwide internet shutdown for several weeks in July 2020, and that communications blackouts have been reported in the Tigray and neighbouring regions since November 2022.
evidence_summary: The profile's section on freedom of the media and access to information reports that during national high school exams it is common for the government to openly block social media sites or to shut down telecom and internet services, that since November 2022 communications blackouts have been reported in the Tigray and neighbouring regions, and that government authorities imposed a nationwide internet shutdown for several weeks in July 2020.
source_excerpt: During national high school exams, it is common for the government to openly block some social media sites like Telegram or to shut down telecom and internet services... Since November 2022, communications blackouts have been reported in the Tigray and neighbouring regions. Similarly, government authorities imposed a nationwide internet shutdown for several weeks in July 2020.
interpretation: Institutional-report evidence documenting reported state practice of restricting access to digital communications (social media blocking and internet shutdowns), presented by an independent intergovernmental agency. It is reporting of observed practice as of the report date (early 2024); it does not independently adjudicate legality.
citation: UNECA, 'Digital Trade Country Profile: Ethiopia' (2024), p.6.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the UNECA country profile (freedom of the media and access to information section).
relevant_policy_or_law: Freedom of the Mass Media and Access to Information Proclamation No. 590/2008
keywords: internet shutdown, social media blocking, media freedom, transparency, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/10/eth-country-profile-en.pdf).

title: UNECA: before 2024 no legislation regulated cross-border data flows in Ethiopia
publisher_or_author: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)
institution: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
claim: UNECA's digital trade country profile states that with no legislation regulating cross-border data flows, data could be transferred abroad from Ethiopia without the need to meet any legal requirement, and that firms were not obligated to adopt procedures incorporating accountability principles or other procedures safeguarding cross-border data transfers.
evidence_summary: The profile's data flows section reports that with no legislation regulating cross-border data flows, data can be transferred abroad without the need to meet any legal requirement, and thus firms are not obligated to adopt procedures incorporating accountability principles or other procedures safeguarding cross-border data transfers.
source_excerpt: With no legislation regulating cross-border data flows, data can be transferred abroad without the need to meet any legal requirement. Thus, firms are not obligated to adopt procedures incorporating accountability principles or other procedures safeguarding cross-border data transfers.
interpretation: Time-limited evidence: documents the legal state as of the report date (early 2024), i.e. the absence of a statutory cross-border data transfer regime before the Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 (gazetted 24 July 2024) introduced a territorial storage mandate and prior-approval cross-border transfer regime (Art. 22). Complements, rather than contradicts, ev2: it describes the earlier legal state.
citation: UNECA, 'Digital Trade Country Profile: Ethiopia' (2024), p.6.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the UNECA country profile (cross-border data flows discussion).
relevant_policy_or_law: Personal Data Protection Proclamation No. 1321/2024 (post-dates this report)
keywords: cross-border data flows, data localization, data protection, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/10/eth-country-profile-en.pdf). Temporal sequence with ev2 (PDP 1321/2024) noted in interpretation.

title: UNECA: interconnection between telecom providers is regulated in Ethiopia
publisher_or_author: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa (UNECA)
institution: United Nations Economic Commission for Africa
claim: UNECA's digital trade country profile reports that interconnection - links or connections between telecommunication service providers allowing users of one supplier to communicate with users of other suppliers - is regulated in Ethiopia by the Communication Services Proclamation No. 1148/2019, its Articles 42 and 43, and the Interconnection Directive No. 791/2021.
evidence_summary: The profile's section on access to infrastructure and connectivity defines interconnection as links or connections between telecommunication service providers that allow users of one supplier to communicate with users of other suppliers and access their services, notes that interconnection is key to competition and commonly regulated, and states that the Communication Services Proclamation No. 1148/2019 and its implementing directives regulate access to infrastructure and connectivity, with Articles 42 and 43 of the proclamation and the Interconnection Directive No. 791/2021 covering interconnection fees and processes.
source_excerpt: Interconnection refers to links or connections between telecommunication service providers that allow users of one supplier to communicate with users of other suppliers and access their services. Interconnection is key to competition between telecom service providers and is commonly regulated to promote fair competition and prevent abuse by dominant firms. Communication Services Proclamation No. 1148/2019 and its implementing directives regulate access to infrastructure and connectivity. Articles 42 and 43 of the proclamation and the Interconnection Directive No. 791/2021 regulate interconnection fees and processes and require operators to make reference offers public.
interpretation: Institutional-report evidence describing the regulatory framework for network interconnection (a form of digital infrastructure interoperability) in Ethiopia. It is an agency description of the legal regime and does not itself assess the implementation or effectiveness of interconnection in practice.
citation: UNECA, 'Digital Trade Country Profile: Ethiopia' (2024), p.4.
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the UNECA country profile (access to infrastructure and connectivity section).
relevant_policy_or_law: Communication Services Proclamation No. 1148/2019; Interconnection Directive No. 791/2021
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/10/eth-country-profile-en.pdf).
